recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Bio: Steven A. Young holds an MSci and a PhD in theoretical physics, and now describes himself as an author, musician and natural philosopher. He is the author of A Fool's Wisdom: Science Conspiracies & The Secret Art of Alchemy, which critiques scientific materialism before presenting Hermetic alchemy as a science of transformation. Under the alias Hedflux he has produced electronic music since 2003, going full time in 2010 and founding the label Luminus Music, with a body of work collected in a 20 Year Legacy Collection of 88 tracks and 12 DJ mixes. He lives in Scotland, where he teaches Audio Alchemy, a synthesis of musical, scientific and Hermetic knowledge.
recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Name: Steven Young

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Creativity as the Spiritual Path", "body": "Chance opens on his long held view that the mystery of the generative power sits at the core of all mythology, religion and science, and Steven Young answers that as a working physicist he never had to be creative, only to study and respond to what he was taught. Becoming a full time artist, facing the question of what to create each day, is what moved him from a belief in evolution to creationism and on to alchemy. Chance recalls the emptiness he felt after college until he began making things, and calls creativity the one universal spiritual path, a way of imitating the creator of the cosmos."}, {"title": "Why Theoretical Physics Produces Nothing", "body": "Steve describes being drawn to quantum physics as the capstone of the academic pyramid, starting in astrophysics, switching to theoretical physics in his third year and staying on for a PhD. Twenty years later he says he cannot name a single real world application of atomic theory, quantum physics, relativity or gravity. He separates the positive sciences like engineering, medicine and chemistry, which build and fix things, from a negative science of models and equations that never has to produce anything, and he pictures millions of minds and billions of gigaflops spent every year on fruitless calculations, while many fellow PhD students were simply aiming for investment banking."}, {"title": "Power, Secrets and the True Sciences", "body": "Steve points to a counterintelligence effort, and when Chance reads a line from Steve's book saying the conspiracy behind physics is all about power and secrets, Steve ties it to blackmail, where people are tempted, entrapped and filmed so that the most compromised rise to the top and can be steered from the shadows. Against that, Steve names astrology as the true science of the stars and alchemy as the true science of earth, soul sciences of working with your hands and purifying yourself, which he says students are taught to sneer at while being handed astronomy and chemistry instead."}, {"title": "The Pseudoscientific Tower of Babel", "body": "Chance puts up his redrawn version of the graphic from Steve's book, which Mark Gober has since named Young's Framework of Social Engineering. Steve walks it down from COVID through superbugs, vaccination, germ theory and evolution, then explains how evolution rests on gravity, gravity on heliocentrism, and both on the atom, since the solar system is drawn on the same model as the atom. He argues atomism makes everything real separate from everything else and once justified hedonism among the ancient atomists, while Chance points to the ground floor beneath the tower, music, alchemy, agriculture and natural law, and reads the Big Bang as the old cosmic egg."}, {"title": "Nukes, Particles and the Four Forces", "body": "Asked directly about nukes, Steve says Hiroshima and Nagasaki were rebuilt soon after the bombs and that Chernobyl kept operating for years, and he cites Galen Windsor, who handled uranium and plutonium with no harm he could see. Steve argues Geiger counters register a frequency of radiation rather than particles, that dropping particles dissolves the famous paradoxes, and that of the four fundamental forces only electromagnetism is real. Chance notes that CERN shares its consonants with Kronos, and Steve closes the free hour saying there is no limit to how big a chemical bomb can be, but that nuclear fallout is a myth used to frighten people."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Is modern physics a collection of theoretical myths? Steven Young, a PhD nuclear physicist, joins the InnerVerse to dismantle the "Tower of Babel" that is modern scientism. From the refutation of Atomism and Nuclear Myth to the "Space Sex Hex," we are peeling back the layers of worldview warfare to find the truth underneath.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Steven Young (Hedflux) shares his journey from the heart of the academic establishment to becoming a musical alchemist. We decode why "Young’s Framework" proves that modern science doesn't produce "fruit," but instead creates a nihilistic separation between the soul and the cosmos.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Uranium as Heavy Lead", "body": "Steven Young traces uranium to pitchblende, an ore that carries lead and uranium together, and notes that physics itself says uranium decays into lead. His reading is that uranium is simply a heavier, charged lead that holds fire inside the metal and releases it slowly, like a bell ringing out. A nuclear power station, on this view, is hot metal rods heating water into steam, and the bomb is a very large chemical explosion using a dense fuel. He sees the nuclear scare, a phrase he takes from Galen Windsor, as a way to keep powerful radiant metals out of ordinary hands."}, {"title": "Jargon as a Spell", "body": "Chance argues that power differentials have always been guarded by jargon, noting that the word technology points back to the terms of a trade, and he wonders whether the story of radioactive materials and the vocabulary of neuroscience work partly through a nocebo effect. Steve calls nuclear terminology a set of spells that rename fire and earth as photons, neutrinos, carbon and atoms, when it is all solids, liquids, gases and heat. He adds that synapses, receptors and the blood brain barrier rest on accepted models rather than evidence, and Chance answers with biofield tuning, where memories turn up in the field around the body, organized like a filing cabinet."}, {"title": "Holy Harmony and True Healing", "body": "Steve decoded a Latin inscription on a roughly 400 year old alchemical artwork that reads holy harmony is the flight of all evils, and he connects it to church bells. St Andrews still rings its bell every hour and feels vibrant, he says, while Dundee, a short trip north, has silent churches and a city in decline. He contrasts healing through vibration, hands, water, fire and plant medicine with a healthcare system built like war, with scalpels, needles and drugs. For inflammation, an excess of fire, the alchemical approach is to stop the action causing it and balance it with cooling, moistening qualities."}, {"title": "Questioning the Hawking Story", "body": "Steve says his chapter on Stephen Hawking is the one readers privately tell him they love, even though interviewers never raise it. He retraces a 2019 Daily Mail piece about a puppet theory, a 1985 conference in Geneva after which Hawking dropped out of sight for about a year, and his return with a voice computer and a new book. He finds it strange that Hawking later married the wife of the engineer who built that computer, and the two ask who actually programmed its preset phrases. Steve also wonders what colleagues such as Roger Penrose knew and never said."}, {"title": "The Globe, the Egg and the Band", "body": "Steve describes coming to globe skepticism around 2016 and waiting years before speaking publicly, and he tells of freezing a gyroscope before long flights, such as Hawaii to the American east coast, and finding it never shifted. Once faith in the space program collapses, he argues, the theory alone cannot hold the globe together. Chance shares a painting of a cosmic egg with concentric rings of land, Venus and Mars as the sun and moon of an outer ring, and Mercury as a luminary near the center. Steve notes the overhead sun only reaches between 66 degrees north and south, and air travel stays inside that band."}]
